notes.title: Alpha 2r3.1 Hotfixes for Collision & Stage loading error
notes.content: [p]This hotfix addresses a number of reported and observed issues with Friday's release of Alpha2r3 Demo Update.[/p][p][/p][h2]Bug Fixes[/h2][list][*][p][b]Stage Loading[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue with stages loaded after the first game session were not properly activating collision objects as they were coming on screen[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Enemies[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Hauler enemy collision would not damage the player[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Spinning enemy collision would not damage the player[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Centipedes would not take damage from Bombs[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Vulcan Sentry and Centipede would not flash when taking damage[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Visuals[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed a rendering issue with 3D parallax effect causing grainy display at higher resolutions[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with the background pillar parallax effect in Shipyard 7 was moving in the opposite direction than intended[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with background holes in Shipyard 7 not being displayed[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where option drones were not changing layers when rotating around the player[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Steam Leaderboard[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where network disconnect caused Game Over screen to hang while waiting for timeout to Steam Servers, preventing continuing or exiting until timeout was over.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Performance[/h2][list][*][p][b]Tilemaps[/b][/p][list][*][p]Incremental loading of tilemaps has been improved with a new system of loading and resampling spline curves incrementally.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Known Issues[/h2][list][*][p]Stage Scoring Screen for Shipyard 7 is not tracking enemy kills correctly. Related to player-level tracking and high scores.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy Missiles that are destroyed by the player can still cause splash damage to the player, this is not intended as the splash damage should instead damage enemies when player destroys them.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Alpha 2r3 - Steam Deck, Performance & Visual Improvements
notes.content: [p]This update is much more technical than the previous updates. It brings much improved performance to Cosmic Destroyer, particularly for low-end PCs that don't have dedicated GPUs. While we still recommend a dedicated GPU for the game, I feel its good to keep the game running as smoothly as possible on lower-spec systems.[/p][p][/p][p]There's a new parallax effect in this update which adds a 3D effect to the edge of environmental objects, including large asteroids and station interiors. It looks really cool and has been optimized to run well even on older hardware.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/fb9e33724cbede5fc7bda55a8d700ffdac145fbe.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Also, last week's update brought the new Grappling Hook to the game, I didn't get a chance to mention it in the release announcement. But I'm still super excited about this feature so I'd like to mention it now! [/p][p]Grabbing enemies has always been a favorite feature among all players, and now its been enhanced to allow grabbing enemies from further away. This also helps the player "test" whats grab-able and not. Use it to grab enemies, objects, and power-ups.[/p][p][/p][p]I can't wait to add more hidden power-ups, pickups, and other fun things to grab and play with.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/86a14e0e2f1b87c9e8e50f4d5ec932ce50e62ebb.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Did you know?[/h3][p]Held enemies provide bonus synergies to your ship! Held popcorn enemies (Blue+Green, Purple Drones) will turret fire at nearby enemies. Interceptors like these in Shipyard 7 provide a big speed boost while held. There's also a shield synergy and some mechanics I'm playing with related to bomb/special behaviors while certain objects are held![/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Steam Deck & Linux Performance[/h2][p]Steam Deck and Linux (Vulkan rendering) had some issues with texture formats not working for some effects, which has been corrected. Every bullet has a slight distortion trail effect and these should now render properly. Performance of these framebuffer effects has also been greatly improved.[/p][p][/p][p]Techy note: The performance impacts were largely due to Physics island and contact calculation overhead, which has been reduced by over 100x by measurement (a particularly busy scene was improved from 14ms on single frame scene down to 0.08 on older hardware). [/p][p][/p][h2]Notable Changes & Improvements[/h2][list][*][p]Ship speeds have been tweaked. VSpec Mk. I and Prototype L-1 have a speed of 6 (down from 7) and the E.M.A has a speed of 7.5. In the future speed and other stat values will be displayed on the ship selection screen[/p][/*][*][p]Intro section on Grid 38 (Stage 1) has been extended. It should be noted that nothing other than the enemies is collidable here, it is purely intended as a fast-paced launch sequence intro.[/p][/*][*][p]Deadzone Camera feature - a deadzone camera that only moves when player is near the edge of the screen. This can be turned on and off in the options menu, the Deadzone camera is now the default camera behavior based on player feedback - it feels much less "floaty".[/p][/*][*][p]Dialogue in the Briefing no longer auto-advances. Players can move to the next dialogue line or skip the dialogue by holding Cancle/Bomb. This was requested by many players who did not have time to finish reading the dialogue. (This will only apply to non-arcade builds as no pausing will be allowed in true arcade setups)[/p][/*][*][p]A new Parallax effect has been added to the game that creates a 3D effect to the edges of pixel art, and has been applied to environmental objects. This effect will be tweaked, improved and added to additional objects in the future. Still working on a secondary variant effect for distant objects.[/p][/*][*][p]Stage Select screen visuals have been improved. [/p][list][*][p]Background elements have been added to match the Briefing Screen, calling out Grid 38, Shipyard 7 and Rossgate Colonly.[/p][/*][*][p]Ship on the map screen now matches the player's current ship instead of a generic one.[/p][/*][*][p]Moving to new stage animation has been improved, no longer snaps when starting to move[/p][/*][*][p]Stage Select screen bug affecting the display of the map paths if resolutions were changed has been corrected[/p][/*][*][p]Stage Select screen button prompts have been added[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Scanline Improvments[/p][list][*][p]Scanlines were not being applied correctly due to a material reference error. All Scanlines were always 2X and not using the profiles for intensity that had been configured. This has been corrected[/p][/*][*][p]Scanline effect accuracy has been improved for resolutions that are not even multiples of the game internal resolution.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Audio[/p][list][*][p]Audio Clips on explosions have been corrected to allow for spatial mixing[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Bugs[/p][list][*][p]Fixed a bug when no enemies were killed in a stage caused an error[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where dropdowns would not scroll to the next element properly when navigating via keyboard or joystick[/p][/*][*][p]A Minimum resolution (640x480) has been imposed to prevent issues where the UI is too large to be displayed, thus locking the player out of menu navigation.[/p][/*][*][p]Duplicate resolutions in the option menu have been removed[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Score Popups would appear on top of the Stage Clear Score Summary screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Multiple environmental bugs have been corrected that prevented some elements from displaying at all.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Known Issues[/h2][list][*][p]There is still a perceivable hit to performance when first encountering the Vulcan Cannon Sentry on Shipyard 7's entrance. This is a level streaming performance hit that is currently being worked on.[/p][/*][*][p]The new Deadzone camera can cause a different type of annoying camera issue when playing Co-Op. Since players can go off screen vertically currently, I will be implementing a shared camera target to reduce camera bounciness in Co-Op.[/p][/*][*][p]Some grabbed enemies and objects are destroyed while being pulled in by the grappling hook due to touching the environment.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Alpha 2r2 - New Ship, Plasma Link Weapon, Auto Fire feature and more
notes.content: [p]Alpha 2r2 is finally here! This patch brings a massive list of improvements and bug fixes to Cosmic Destroyer and some new Features![/p][p]I spent the weekend demoing Cosmic Destroyer at 2D Con, and the prep for the convention delayed the planned release until today. So much good feedback and new bug fixes to get into the release that I felt it was better to release all of these updates together. I apologize for any inconvenience if you were hoping to play Cosmic Destroyer's new update last weekend and experienced the old bugs! [/p][p][/p][h1]Notable Features and Changes[/h1][p][/p][h2]New Ship - E.M.A.[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/a9eb83d3eabe740c62d93bdcea5bad2205142ba5.gif"][/img][/p][p]The E.M.A. is an Electro-Magnetic Assault ship. It zaps everything in its way with a Plasma Link weapon that leaps like chain lightning! Its available immediately for players to try it out. It will no doubt need some re-balancing in the future - as part of a re-balance coming to all ships and enemies.[/p][p][/p][h2]Auto Fire Functionality[/h2][p]The community asked for it, and it's here! Auto Fire is fully emulated based on old-school hardware techniques. This new fire mode can be configured to trigger at 60hz, 30hz or 15hz and allows the player to hold the button to fire wide shots while continuing to move quickly. Fire control for the focus shot has not been modified, so there are two fire buttons.[/p][p][/p][p]Players can also hold the Focus Shot button to move slowly while sustaining auto-fire wide shot[/p][p][/p][h2]Grab and Throw Enemies and Objects[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/0ca02ddaedf8973a813039169c0b6333b2737471.gif"][/img][/p][p]You can now grab and throw both small enemies and objects! These are some of the strongest attacks in the entire game by design, and will also be used for keys, batteries and other items to open up alternate paths in the future. (Also shown here, improved visibility of the fast-moving purple projectiles)[/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, held enemies provide a synergy ability when held.[/p][list][*][p]Green Popcorn Drone & Purple Hangar Drone - Turrets attacks towards nearby enemies[/p][/*][*][p]Interceptor - Provides a Speed Bonus when held[/p][/*][*][p]Slug Larvae (Enemy Coming Soon) - Adds a bullet-slowing effect around the player when the player is firing a focus shot.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][h2]New Starfield[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/67f2891564d4042b4161400b4d88a9a71153e7ee.gif"][/img][/p][p]It's the little things that really add up. The starfield effect that was being used previously was a simple particle effect with positioning each frame, but this had many limitations and stylistically didn't really fit the pixel art aesthetic. It also had some really wonky artifacts when stages were twisting and turning. [/p][p]The new starfield uses dynamically layered sprites which stretch while keeping each star's burst effect. The result is a much more consistent visual which is also much more performant and reliable.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]Gameplay Improvements and Adjustments[/h2][list][*][p]Auto Fire functionality has been added. This feature emulates old-school hardware Auto Fire, which triggers the press action of the main shot at a configurable rate. You will find options for 15hz, 30hz, and 60hz Auto Fire in the Controls page of the Options menu along with button mapping for the Auto Fire (defaults to North Button (Y/Triangle) on gamepads and V on keyboard mapping).[/p][/*][*][p]Pacing of Stage 1 has been adjusted to be a bit more forgiving in the opening sections.[/p][list][*][p] First spread turret has been replaced with a normal turret[/p][/*][*][p]One ship hangar has been removed[/p][/*][*][p]Spinning Enemies which come from behind don't appear until later in the stage.[/p][/*][*][p]Laser Corvette in cave section has been removed as this was too near a wide turn, which resulted in wide laser sweep that was largely unavoidable[/p][/*][*][p]Breakable blocks have been added to the exit of the asteroid base to allow a player to pass through.[/p][/*][*][p]Overall speed has been tweaked across the stage[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Grazing projectile velocities have been improved, with dynamic behavior based on different projectile types allowing for some projectiles to inherit part of their original velocity (such as Purple shots from turrets).[/p][/*][*][p]Interceptor Enemy Ship provides a speed bonus to the player when held.[/p][/*][*][p]Popcorn Drone Enemy Ship provides a turreting ability when held which prioritizes enemies, then asteroids[/p][/*][*][p]Gamepad Deadzones have been improved to prevent bounce in UI menus. Specific deadzones have been set for both Xbox and Playstation controllers respectively.[/p][/*][*][p]Steam Input detection has been added. The game is not intended to be used with Steam Input for controllers other than Steam Controller. The game provides its own support for all major controllers. If a player has Steam Input enabled and is not using an actual Steam Controller, a popup is shown to recommend disabling Steam Input.[/p][/*][*][p]Ship Selection can now be done with a mouse click.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted Sable's dialogue at the start of Shipyard 7 stage to be a bit shorter and more clear.[/p][/*][*][p]Reactor Turbine no longer uses collision triggers to start its mini-cutscene, this is much more reliable and works for Co-Op even if players die just before the cutscene starts.[/p][/*][*][p]Stage Loading and general object instantiation performance has been improved across the board, this reduces lost frames while streaming stage assets during play as well.[/p][/*][*][p]A new developer tool to ensure all collision areas are pixel-aligned has been created, and colliders have been edited using this tool to improve consistency[/p][/*][*][p]Smoother rotations through stages. Spline Arc Parameterization performance has been improved by adding spatial partitioning, allowing the accuracy to be improved by over 5 times and spline lookup. As a baseline performance measure, stage 1 spline lookup has been improved from 3-4ms down to 0.02ms.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Visual Improvements[/h2][list][*][p]Starfield background has been improved to handle rotations much more accurately, allowing for more varied parallaxing effects.[/p][/*][*][p]Visual clarity of some tiles which are collidable have been improved to be more obvious to the player.[/p][/*][*][p]Visual clarity of the Crane Miniboss has been improved by changing palette from orange to a cooler pale green. Bullets are much more readable on this screen now.[/p][/*][*][p]Fast moving Purple Bullets now have an outline flash effect to enhance bullet readability. The darker purple was hard to track on some brown and blue backgrounds.[/p][/*][*][p]Score Summary screen has been improved to roll-up the enemies with a counter showing "Destroyed / All" for each enemy type.[/p][list][*][p]This includes new sprites for all enemies in the score summary screen to prevent stretching.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Bug Fixes[/h2][list][*][p]Fixed a major collision issue where player's Option Drone can collide with some world objects such as doors which caused unexpected damage to player. No more "I died for no reason"![/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a codec issue with Arcade Marquee / Attract Screen video not playing on Linux and older Windows computers[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a performance issue with parallax spline background elements[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue in Shipyard 7 stage where the next section of the stage would sometimes not load after the Vulcan Sentry enemy[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with navigation in the Controls section of the Options Menu[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed all dropdown menu items in the options menu so that the selected option is highlighted when opened or new items are selected with keyboard or joystick[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with UI elements remaining highlighted from the mouse after navigation by keyboard or joystick selects a different item[/p][/*][*][p]Collision issues in the Shipyard 7 stage have been corrected, including[/p][list][*][p]Assembly Line Area[/p][/*][*][p]Centipede Nest[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fixed issue with Centipede legs sometimes stacking in the wrong order[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a control issue with moving from the Tutorial stage to the Briefing and Ship Selection screens, where tutorial would start over instead of going to Stage 1[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with some popcorn enemies not initializing in Stage 1, causing them to remain stationary[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an error which occurred when thrown asteroids collided with other asteroids due to having no Entity ID to register damage for score summary screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where held enemies would take damage from bombs[/p][/*][/list][h2]Known Issues[/h2][list][*][p]Tutorial still has some issues with pacing and is currently being reworked into much quicker sections for the basic controls.[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies are simply wiped at the end of the stage which can look a bit jarring. The plan is to disable their collision and firing behaviors and provide transition behaviors for the stage end event (such as the Space Jet boss boosting off the screen if needed)[/p][/*][*][p]Many players have requested that gamepad triggers be mapped by default for firing, bombs and grabbing. This may require addition of a 3rd control mapping to retain functionality for having keyboard and gamepad mappings mapped simultaneously. Otherwise keyboard and gamepad mapping may need to be separated.[/p][/*][*][p]Control Mapping does not prevent the user from assigning the same button to multiple actions. It would be best to display a prompt to user that the control is already mapped and allow override/cancel of the remapping.[/p][/*][*][p]Audio mix levels change slightly in the main menu, which can cause a jump in audio levels when going to the options menu, which changes the audio mix abruptly.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Alpha v2 Released - Shipyard 7 Infestation
notes.content: [h1]Alpha 2 Demo has been Released![/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/92b3f8f0778b6ac568f89f5464f04157b5ecb19c.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This update brings all the features from last week's closed testing to the public demo - which includes a ton of new features, a teaser of the next stage's Interceptor production line area, 4 new enemies, and a quick look at a new massive mini-boss.[/p][list][*][p]Grab and Throw small enemies,[/p][/*][*][p]New Enemies - Interceptor, Light Cruiser and Missile Cruiser, and some creepy crawly centipedes[/p][/*][*][p]Bullet Grazing and Bullet Sealing mechanics[/p][/*][*][p]New Scoring Mechanics[/p][/*][*][p]Entirely new areas and environments - Assembly plant with working conveyors and pneumatic stamping machines (smashers), and a centipede nest.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/27f13efd8b395ebf08dea9e2f0a66a4d1abd8c85.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/0ddab2086040450d20f3536c58d26c81611f6653.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This is really just the beginning as far as what's to come in Cosmic Destroyer - new areas, a re-balance including more ships and weapons are just the around the corner - stay tuned as more features are coming very soon! Follow [url="https://bsky.app/profile/coffeemakergames.bsky.social"]CoffeeMakerGames [/url]on Bluesky for live updates.[/p][p][/p][p]More details on the features included in the Alpha 2 release can be found in the dev roadmap update from last week:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3712340/view/541113388287132111?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Game Mechanics Update and Dev Roadmap - (Alpha 1r2)
notes.content: [h2]A cargo hold full of new features are coming![/h2][p]This update is available to closed beta users and will be rolled out to the public demo [b]next week on 8/14/25[/b]. The update is focused on adding a host of new game mechanics, and brings exciting updates to cover in detail. This includes updates to Grabbing, a new Missile type, Bullet Sealing and Grazing, as well as a complete overhaul of scoring mechanics and menu systems.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Where is Cosmic Destroyer Headed?[/h2][p]I am very excited to be charging towards [b]2DCON on August 22nd to 24th in Minnesota[/b], where Cosmic Destroyer will be on demo at our booth on the Indie Island.[/p][p]Here is a quick overview of the current development timeline for the next few weeks, which will bring more major updates [b]every Thursday up to August 21st![/b] There are even more exciting features planned, including an update to the Steam demo for Cosmic Destroyer on 8/14/2025 which will include a teaser of the new Shipyard 7 Stage – a nearby military installation constructing powerful ships for the defense of civilian colonies in the belt. It’s also the incursion point for the enemy force from the unknown.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/17aed22dac7129133c0c95d25e5ecc809d9ffd41.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The plan going forward is to have a steady stream of updates with releases and roadmap updates every two weeks. Stay tuned for more updates, news, features. [b]The ultimate goal is to release the full version of the game before the end of 2025![/b][/p][p] [/p][h3]Grabbing and Tossing Enemies[/h3][p]Small enemies such as Mining Drones, Scout Pods and Interceptors can now be grabbed just like special weapons by pressing the action button. [/p][p]A held enemy will provide special abilities based on the enemy type. These abilities range from firing at other enemies like a turret, altering your ship’s Primary or Secondary Weapons, or providing completely new abilities. You can also hold the action button after grabbing an enemy to charge up a throw maneuver which is being considered for other charge-up abilities as well! If that wasn’t enough, the enemy can be rammed into other enemies and used to protect your ship from projectiles while held.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/21eecc89d4c6f6e18a4f83e92e1a28be0bb4eaa7.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h3]New Secondary Weapon: Lock On Missiles[/h3][p]This new secondary weapon locks-on to enemies within an area in front of the player’s ship while the fire button is held down. During that time, a lock-on reticle will be shown over targeted enemies. Upon release of the fire button, missiles are fired at each of the targets. These missiles trade stopping power for versatility, and are particularly well suited to hitting targets which are moving or positioned vertically in relation to the player. The maximum number of targets increases with missile power level and missile power-ups now cycle between the missile types which are available in the current game. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/2c06f83a3491a6818379658d1ade9c68ed95c7dc.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In [b]Arcade Mode[/b] these power-ups will cycle as follows:[/p][list][*][p][b]“M” Power-Up[/b] – Adds a missile of the current equipped type. If no missile was previously equipped, the default missile type for the ship will be used (generally Dumbfire Missiles).[/p][/*][*][p][b]“D” Power-Up[/b] – Switches to Dumbfire Missiles. If Dumbfire Missiles are already equipped the power level is increased, adding an additional missile. If another missile type is currently equipped, the missile power is reset to 1[/p][/*][*][p][b]“L” Power-Up[/b] – Switches to Lock-On Missiles. If Lock-On Missiles are already equipped the power level is increased, adding additional missile(s). If another missile type is currently equipped, the missile power is reset to 1[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][i]Note: some enemies being introduced soon will also fire Lock-On missiles which can be shot and destroyed. Missiles cannot be absorbed or grazed like normal bullets as they detonate when near a target and apply damage in an area.[/i][/p][p] [/p][h3]Option Drone Power-Up Behavior[/h3][p]Option Drones currently provide a small score boost when they absorb an enemy projectile. Additionally, option drones which have absorbed a projectile become powered up for a limited duration, which increases based on the player’s Hit Multiplier. The projectiles fired from an empowered drone have a larger hit detection box and graphic, and do bonus damage. Option drones which collide with enemies and boss cores inflict damage, and this damage is also increased while powered-up.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/b919e723f585074d23cdc5015dfa8dc6181255e0.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p] [/p][h3]Bullet Sealing[/h3][p]Getting up close and firing point-blank at an enemy is a risk which should be rewarded, not punished. While this was always planned, we’ve heard your feedback and have implemented this mechanic. Point-blanking bosses and spinning turrets is no longer certain death. Enemy firing logic will not create bullets if the player is right on top of them. This does not apply to charged lasers and other telegraphed special attacks such as jetstreams, flames, and missiles. The strategy of point-blanking works great with the damage buffs to option drone collisions and skilled players can use this dangerous strategy to maximize damage and take down enemies quickly.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Bullet Grazing[/h2][p]Bullet grazing mechanics allow a player to narrowly dodge a projectile to get an added bonus effect. This is generally reflecting the projectile back at a nearby enemy, which does heavy damage. Spread shots can be a powerful countermeasure to a screen filled with enemies – and this risk-reward pays off! In the future, we’d like to introduce more player choice to this mechanic, to allow players to chose the effect when grazing. These concepts range from trading reflected bullets for additional scoring, temporary power-ups, and temporary shields just to name a few.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/e98fbbeded88f8b5218068cb98ec761948d854fc.gif"][/img][/p][p]A bit of a tease of the first area of the new stage "Shipyard 7" and some of the ships. This stage will be [b]playable in the demo update coming next week on 8/14/25[/b].[/p][p][/p][h2]New Scoring Mechanics[/h2][p]In addition to the score pickups found in ground objects and when destroying complete enemy waves, additional score pickups can now be earned based on overall enemy destruction. Every enemy killed by a player is tracked, when enough enemies have been killed, a special score pickup is created which automatically is pulled into the player. The number of enemies required to spawn this score pickup is determined by the player’s current hit multiplier. The higher the multiplier, the fewer the number of enemies required to create a score pickup. Since the multiplier also applies to these pickups, this further incentivizes the player to make every effort to keep their hit multiplier high – because racking up a high score not only contributes to the leaderboard score but also results in additional lives at 50,000, 200,000 and 1,000,000 points.[/p][p] [/p][p]There are a few more changes to mention related to scoring:[/p][list][*][p]Each player’s Hit Multiplier no longer drains while transitions are occurring – as this was just not fair. It’s intended to be possible to complete all stages without ever losing your score multiplier.[/p][/*][*][p]Hit multipliers over 4X periodically create additional power-ups when enemies are defeated. Picking up a power-up which is already maxed-out provides a 100 point bonus (multiplied by hit multiplier, this is a substantial bonus).[/p][/*][*][p]Scoring bonuses are applied upon completion of the stage based on performance, which is outlined in “New Score Summary Screen”.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2]New Score Summary Screen[/h2][p]At the end of a stage, each player is now shown a progress report for the completed stage. This includes a roll-up of the following metrics, as well as bonus points awarded for performance in each area:[/p][list][*][p]Ships Lost – A player which manages to complete a stage without losing a single ship is awarded a hefty reward of 10,000 points.[/p][/*][*][p]Bullets Canceled – Bullets cancelled either by grazing or special abilities such as power bombs are tracked here. 10 Points are awarded for each cancel[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies Defeated – Each enemy gives points when it is destroyed, but an additional bonus is given when reaching the end of the stage for all enemies. This bonus is 10 points per enemy. Additionally, if a high percentage of enemies are destroyed the player is awarded additional large bonuses:[/p][list][*][p]100% Destruction – 100,000 points![/p][/*][*][p]98% Destruction – 25,000 points[/p][/*][*][p]95% Destruction – 10,000 points[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Enemies Defeated Visual Summary – All enemies encountered in the stage are shown as visual representation at the bottom of the scoring screen, each defeated enemy is shown as a darker version when defeated.[/p][list][*][p]Objects like asteroids are grouped into one entry and may be removed from the “Enemies” classification in the future – as the only realistic way to destroy them all currently is by using bombs.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Finally, all totals for the stage are rolled-up and applied to the player’s total score for the current game session.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/6f1bb22c1b5adc554715779d185d3962bf6d7df6.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][p][i]Reminder: Using a continue currently resets the player’s current score to zero when it is used. This is for the purpose of embracing the 1CC (One Credit Clear) goal of many skilled SHMUP players. In the future the plan is to replace this logic with flags for 1CC completions, which will have their own separate Leaderboard. We want to track each stage’s scoring and the over-all game session scoring non-destructively so players can see their score history in the future.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]Menu Overhaul and UI Improvements[/h2][p]The entire menu system logic, as well as the visual style of menus has been overhauled to provide a better and more consistent experience. This also enables development of more dynamic menu layouts and flows in the future, and ability to configure and customize  menu style in the future.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/4887254afef1af27df991da1be52deaa4fdb2b1c.gif"][/img][/p][p] [/p][h2]Projectile Pattern and Enemy Spawn Determinism[/h2][p]Previously, when bullet patterns and enemies were spawned on the screen, their behavior could be inconsistent on different devices or depending on system performance. This was because the system was starting the logic for these entities based on the position of the object relative to the current scroll position of the stage, which could happen on frames which were not within a fixed, predictable timestep (which is used for behaviors, and physics calculations such as collisions). By ensuring that all projectile patterns and enemy initializations occur at a determined time, a much more consistent player experience can be ensured.[/p][p] [/p][h2]Bug Fixes[/h2][list][*][p]Collision Rework – the methods used for detection of collisions of ships and projectiles has been overhauled to support new grazing features and fix performance and false-positive collision bugs.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an error where the options menu remained active while closed.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with game scroll position being inconsistent[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where stages would display slightly differently for users on Steam Deck or Linux compared to Windows. Arc Parameterization for splines has been overhauled to be more consistent when calculating rotation regardless of platform.[/p][/*][/list][p] [/p][h2]Platform Updates[/h2][list][*][p]Major performance improvements to Ship Manager and Projectile Managers, allowing for a 30-35% boost to maximum frame rate in busy scenes.[/p][/*][*][p]Future support for Alternate Game Modes has been added. The entire game’s high-level logic is now hot-pluggable, with systems such as ship loadout behaviors, upgrade paths, stage layout and composition logic all being configurable. This avoids any impact to code needed for other game modes which will be added in the future.[/p][/*][/list][h2] [/h2]

notes.title: Cooperative Multiplayer
notes.content:
I am pleased to announce that Local Cooperative Multiplayer has been added to Cosmic Destroyer! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/be2f423848f95fb11f5a4989a008a1d1bafb4303.png[/img]

[h2]Device Mapping[/h2]
When choosing a game mode from the Main Menu, players can now select Co-Op and will be given the opportunity to choose which devices each player would like to control their ship. This functionality provides flexibility to support multiple devices for users that want to use non-standard setups like bearclaw. During development some very unique setups were tested including one with 2 gamepads, two keyboards and a mouse all working at the same time on one player - and another gamepad on the 2nd player.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/100257b70bfb14080f820b67d120bf3f6b194a8a.png[/img]

Each player can select their favorite ship and ready-up to jump into the game. Both players can select the same ship if they would like, there are no limitations.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/c92d5641b350e10cd522a3c22e9978dce1cfc411.png[/img]

[h2]Multiplayer Gameplay[/h2]

Players have their own store of three lives and three continues, and all stats and scores are separate. When a player has consumed all of their lives they can continue by simply pressing the Action button, provided they have continues left to spend. If both players happen to game over at the same time, the standard Game Over screen will be shown to prompt the last player to continue. This screen is also shown if all lives and continues have been exhausted for both players.

Flair on the ships for each player is colored to match the Player Flag - Player 1 is Red and Player 2 is Blue. This color is also used in the UI HUD indicators in the upper left and upper right, respectively. The boss health indicator has been moved to be positioned at the top of the screen between both HUD elements and should be out of the way.

[h3]Device Disconnections[/h3]
If a device which is currently mapped to a player is disconnected during play, the game will automatically pause. A notification message such as "Playstation Controller has been disconnected" will be displayed on the screen when this occurs. Generally whenever a player uses the pause functionality only that player can unpause or exit gameplay, but in cases of input device disconnection control may switch to the other player to prevent players from getting stuck having to force-quit due to input device issues.


[h3]Other notes and limitations[/h3]
This mode currently does not allow for any High-Scores to be earned and is purely for having fun with your friends locally or using Steam's "Play with Friends" feature, provided a good network connection. Local leaderboards for co-op may be added in the future if there is interest.

Do note that split keyboard setups using one device across multiple players is not currently supported, mostly due to an engine limitation.

[h3]New Story Intro and Tutorial Dialogue[/h3]
Captain Gerson now announces the mission's situation report to you with a virtual briefing before the game starts. The whole team is caught off guard by the initial attack, still the insight and information he provides offers context as to the situation around the Grid 38 Mining Facility and the attack on Shipyard 7. Sable, the ace pilot run the new pilot orientation tutorial, and you'll no doubt see more of her throughout the game. This also includes an ominous new backing track and new dialogue audio effects that really capture that retro feel. As development continues and we get closer to release there will be more information to share and new characters to meet. Although I want to be careful not to spoil anything by revealing too much before the final game release, either!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/f2ac15b34ca565011b3c0b2fdd4eb405e5d743f8.png[/img]

notes.title: Steam Deck and Controller Support
notes.content:
From the beginning of development Steam Deck has been the testing device of choice, and so it only makes sense to do everything to ensure that the game plays well on the Steam Deck both from a control and performance standpoint.

Steam Deck, Xbox, Playstation DualSense and DualShock, Keyboard, and Keyboard-emulated Arcade controller sticks (Specifically the X-Arcade Tankstick) are already tested and working in Cosmic Destroyer.

In addition to other major controller support, Steam Deck requirements are something that is being taken seriously to make sure all the controls work seamlessly. Switching between tapping on the screen or using the joystick buttons or touchpads should just work out of the box in Cosmic Destroyer. The game has it's own control remapping features for the major actions, and these are largely for button mappings and to support arcade stick controllers which operate through keybindings (X-Arcade sticks, etc.). If you need to use Steam Input you can, but you likely won't have to unless you have a non-standard controller (Xbox, Playstation DualShock and DualSense have been tested to work via USB and Bluetooth). If you want to bear-claw between two devices this should mostly work, but efforts have been focused on ensuring things like keyboard+mouse work this way, and Steam Deck controls work when switching between touch screen and joystick. 

As the game has no text input required, other than the score screen which uses the classic arcade input entry - there has been no need to use an on-screen keyboard prompt.

notes.title: Game Options, Settings and Training Mode
notes.content:
Since the initial announcement of Cosmic Destroyer going on Steam earlier this week, my focus has been getting a public demo ready for release for players to try it out. In order for that to really work, players need to be able to configure the game so that it can run properly on their systems. That means that players at the very least need options for display and controls.  Building these option menus and functionality, while vastly improving performance have been the focus of all development effort this week.

Option menus have been added to Cosmic Destroyer to allow players to customize their experience, remap controls and adjust audio and video options. This also includes the addition of a Training Mode for learning the game and the stage layouts, like enemy, power up and destructible object's spawn locations. This is the first of many game modes, expect many more in the coming months as Cosmic Destroyer blasts off towards launch.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/0ece3a20a11de6a33a2011d2c412812b13701382.png[/img]
[h2]Training Mode[/h2]
This mode provides the player with unlimited continues and bombs, and starts the player out with maximum power level, secondary weapons (missiles, etc.) and option drones. When starting a game in Training Mode, the player will be allowed to choose from any starting stage in the final game. Training Mode play-throughs cannot earn achievements or register a high score. A "Training Mode" message callout and watermark are added to the screen.

[h2]Options[/h2]
The following option panels have been added accessible from the main menu.

[h3]Game[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/f2c1df753700ed9a8cab3b7034c67ecf0f7e3702.png[/img]
General game options not related to the current game session/mode are found here
[list]
[*] [b]Show hit box[/b] - shows a brightly colored box exactly matching the size and position of the hit box on the player at all times. This is rendered on top of all other content, even the UI.
[*] [b]Show Hints[/b] - the game often prompts players "Shoot" or "Pick up" the first time they encounter certain objects like cores to shoot to open doors or destroy bosses. This is helpful for new players but can be turned off here.
[*] [b]Show Tutorials[/b] - the first stage involves a section that will wait for player input and introduce a wave of enemies slowly before continuing. This slow progressing section can be disabled here
[*] [b]Arcade Marquee[/b] - A video of gameplay is shown after short time to prevent screen-burn-in and showcase the gameplay. In the future this footage will be replaced with mix of recent high score replays from the player and the top replays from leaderboards. 
[/list]

[h3]Video[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/a87b38a6aadd5f2a60e026d4440acbdb1c09381d.png[/img]
No game is complete without proper video options. The game is intended to be always run at 16:9 resolution, and letterbox / pillarbox is displayed to fill the screen while maintaining a consistent game experience and fair play area to all players regardless of display configuration.
[list]
[*] [b]Display Mode[/b] - options include Windowed Fullscreen, Fullscreen and Windowed
[*] [b]Resolution[/b] - your monitor's resolutions and refresh rate variations can be selected here
[*] [b]V-Sync[/b] - Vertical sync smooths screen tearing when game and monitor refresh speeds do not match
[*] [b]Brightness[/b] - Simple gamma brightness adjustment.
[*] [b]Quality[/b] - (This section is coming soon as it needs a few visual improvements for quality presets) includes options to reduce particle quality such as distortion effects, or reduce particle counts for systems with low-end GPUs which struggle with overlapping transparencies.
[/list]

[h3]Audio[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/d4d6013bfb0e9cc0e97f441f8f0092a1fbc93ca9.png[/img]
We hope you always want to play Cosmic Destroyer at full blast in a loud arcade - but also recognize you might want to play your own music or duck the audio for streaming.
[list]
[*] [b]Main[/b] - Main volume of all sound
[*] [b]SFX[/b] - sound effects such as weapons and explosions
[*] [b]Voice[/b] - announcements such as "Power Up" and "Game Over"
[*] [b]Music[/b] - music, set to however much synthwave you can handle!
[/list]

[h3]Control[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45611288/3cd931b3e3aab906d04891e048e18d40c804f765.png[/img]
Here  you can remap your controls inside the game. Provided are Primary and Secondary mappings with the defaults set to Keyboard and Gamepad bindings. Steam's Mapping should handle scenarios for mapping through that method as well, but provided here to aid with setups such as Keyboard mapped arcade controllers and other customizations.


One last nerdy development note on performance - it's always been a deal-breaker any time the game drops below 60FPS for any reason. It's a "drop everything and fix whatever is causing the slowdown" moment. It is particularly important in these types of games which simulate at their own internal tick of 60FPS. This must be done to ensure reliable movement, collisions, and in the end - scoring. This week, I've also gone through and deeply researched every memory allocation and process time and radically optimized for the smoothest experience possible, to get the game running well even on slower machines. Glad to say that currently, the frame update uses exactly 0 bytes of heap allocation - so NO garbage collection necessary, which avoids random frame drops. On a decent gaming PC I've pushed into well over 200FPS - even when forcing the logic to fully update every single frame. That's good news for anyone who appreciates a smooth gaming experience!
